title: Houthis Claim Large-Scale Missile and Drone Attack on King Khalid Air Base
detail: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed dozens of ballistic missiles and drones struck King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait on Sept 14, 2026, targeting 'aircraft hangars, radar systems, runways, ammunition depots and other military facilities' and causing 'significant losses' — claims not independently confirmed. Saudi Civil Defence issued an alert for Khamis Mushait before saying 'the danger has passed.' The Saudi-led coalition separately reported Houthi drone and missile strikes on Abha and Taif provinces the same day, causing minor injuries and damaging homes and vehicles. The Houthis said the operation was retaliation for more than 300 Saudi airstrikes on Yemen over the preceding five days and warned that further Saudi military action would be met with 'broader and more severe' strikes inside the kingdom.

media.caption: Coverage of the widening Yemen-Saudi escalation following the King Khalid Air Base attack, Sept 2026

title: MBS Meets US CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper in Jeddah
detail: Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman received US Central Command commander Admiral Brad Cooper and his delegation in Jeddah on Sept 14, 2026. Per the Saudi Press Agency, the two sides 'reviewed relations between Saudi Arabia and the US, as well as the latest developments in the region,' with National Security Advisor Musaed Al-Aiban also attending. The meeting came as Houthi attacks on Saudi territory and Red Sea shipping intensified; MBS had earlier sought direct US military assistance against the Houthis from President Trump, but Washington offered intelligence-sharing and targeting support rather than US strikes.

media.caption: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman receives US CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper in Jeddah, Sept 14, 2026
